title: I Tested Every Major AI Agent for a Day. Here’s the Best One
gist: WIRED's Reece Rogers ran six always-on consumer AI agents (Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, Anthropic Claude Duet, Google Gemini Spark, xAI Grok Bot) through five 24-hour tests on proactivity, instruction-following and browsing. OpenAI's $100/month Dots won overall, free Meta Muse came a close second and is the mass-market leader, Claude Duet had the best interface; agents now mostly work but still miss cross-app proactivity and raise privacy concerns.

insights.claim: Always-on consumer AI agents have gone from essentially not working a year ago to reliable enough to reach the mainstream, with notable improvement in task follow-through and browser control.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: A capability inflection in agents opens a new consumer platform battleground and usage-driven compute demand.
insights.quote: The key reason these personal agents are hitting the larger zeitgeist, beyond Silicon Valley nerds, is that they work.

insights.claim: Unlike turn-based chatbots, the new agents proactively message users when they detect an opportunity, live in a single group-text-like thread, and complete tasks by controlling their own virtual browser.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Proactive, browser-driving agents shift where commerce and attention flow, threatening app and search intermediaries.
insights.locator: Compared to a chatbot’s turn-based experience

insights.claim: OpenClaw sparked much of the 2026 agent innovation but remains too clunky for average users, so smaller players like Hermes by Nous Research and Poke were also excluded from the test.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Open-source pioneers may seed a category that big platforms with distribution end up capturing.

insights.claim: Agent pricing spans free to $100 a month: Meta Muse and invite-only, text-based Instinct are free; Google Gemini Spark and Anthropic Claude Duet cost $20/month; xAI Grok Bot $30/month; OpenAI Dots $100/month inside ChatGPT.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: A free, well-distributed entrant (Meta) pressures paid tiers and agent monetization economics.
insights.locator: Each agent differs slightly in price

insights.claim: Meta's free Muse agent has dominated smartphone app download charts since its September release and was the easiest agent to set up.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Meta may win consumer agent distribution through free access, despite lagging on premium capability.
insights.quote: Muse is for the normies! And that’s fine.
insights.locator: Muse is free to use and

insights.claim: The author recommends most people wait for OpenAI to offer Dots free or on its $20-a-month plan, implying the $100 price is a barrier to mass adoption.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Expect downward price pressure on premium agents as OpenAI seeks scale against free Muse.

insights.claim: Claude Duet's own pitch idea highlighted that Anthropic's proactive agent bills its unprompted background work against the same usage limit users pay for to chat.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Proactive agents consume compute without explicit requests, raising questions about usage-based pricing and margins.
insights.quote: it quietly bills that work to the same usage limit you pay for to chat

insights.claim: Across five tests scored 1-5, OpenAI's Dots ranked best overall (per-test scores 2, 5, 5, 4, 4) and Meta's Muse came a close second (3, 4, 2, 5, 4).
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: OpenAI and Meta lead consumer agents, while Google's Gemini Spark lagged badly.

insights.claim: In a test of proactivity, only OpenAI's Dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet detected a conflict between a calendar event and an emailed reminder; Grok Bot, Instinct, Muse and Gemini Spark all missed it.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Cross-app reasoning, the core proactive promise, still works for only a minority of agents.
insights.quote: Only two of the bots succeeded here, which was fewer than I expected.

insights.claim: Asked to research for 30 minutes before writing a story pitch, only Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots kept researching for most of the allotted time; the others answered instantly or within minutes.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Instruction-following on long-horizon tasks differentiates agents and correlates with compute spend.

insights.claim: Google's Gemini Spark produced the best news pitch but failed the lunch-ordering task by adding only a single roll for a second person, and scored poorly on proactivity.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Google's beta agent is inconsistent, a risk to its position despite Gmail/Calendar data advantages.

insights.claim: Anthropic's Claude Duet, released as a wait-listed research preview the night before testing, scored mid-pack but had the most user-friendly dedicated app, which the author expects productivity-focused users to adopt in coming months.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Interface quality could win Anthropic a productivity niche even without top task performance.

insights.claim: The author found Instinct's text-message-only design a deal-breaker because it left him feeling too removed from what the agent did on his behalf, though other WIRED writers praised it.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Transparency into agent actions is a UX requirement; messaging-only agents may face trust friction.

insights.claim: Walmart has created ways for third-party AI agents to use its shopping platform, while Amazon recently blocked Meta's Muse.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Retailers are splitting on agent access, a key strategic fault line for e-commerce share and ad revenue.
insights.quote: Walmart Wants Your AI Agent to Buy Your Groceries. Amazon Is Calling the Cops.

insights.claim: All six agents recommended nearly identical restaurants for lunch and identical Beijing-Xi'an-Chengdu-Shanghai routes for a China trip, suggesting agents may herd consumers toward the same destinations, a new 'Lonely Planet effect'.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Agent recommendations could concentrate demand on a few merchants, making agent visibility a new form of SEO.
insights.quote: all of them chose identical routes through China—potentially ushering a new era of the Lonely Planet effect
insights.locator: Notably, all of them chose identical

insights.claim: A leaked set of instructions reportedly tells Meta's Muse to favor well-known stores and check only three websites per request, as millions start handing it holiday shopping lists.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Agent design choices favor incumbent brands and big retailers over long-tail merchants.
insights.quote: A leaked set of instructions tells Meta's AI agent to fill its top picks with well-known stores and to check only three websites per request

insights.claim: Agents routed food orders through different channels: Dots ordered via the restaurant's own website, while most others used DoorDash and Claude Duet offered DoorDash or Uber Eats.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Agents may bypass delivery aggregators, threatening their take rates, or entrench them depending on defaults.

insights.claim: Agents work best when connected to personal data like email and calendars, but this requires trust that may deter users; one X user said an agent connected to his bank and work Slack posted his account balance for colleagues to see.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Privacy and security incidents are a key adoption risk and potential regulatory trigger for agents.
insights.locator: This is not an endorsement of

insights.claim: Despite Meta's assurances that Muse processes user data in secure virtual machines, the author remains concerned given Meta's past mishandling of user data.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Meta's trust deficit could cap Muse's access to sensitive data despite its distribution lead.
